key_claims: Higher vitamin D supplement intake may be associated with better cognitive function in adults at elevated risk of dementia.
The research was conducted at Emory University.
More than 7 million Americans currently live with Alzheimer's dementia.
The number of Americans with Alzheimer's dementia is projected to reach nearly 13 million by 2050.
limitations: The source does not specify the study design (e.g., randomized controlled trial vs. observational).
The source does not provide details on the population studied, dosage, or duration of supplementation.
The source does not indicate whether the association is causal.
The source does not mention any potential side effects or risks of high-dose vitamin D.
what_not_to_say: Do not claim that vitamin D prevents or treats dementia.
Do not claim that high-dose vitamin D is safe or recommended for everyone.
Do not state specific dosages or durations of supplementation.
Do not generalize findings to all adults, as the study focused on those at elevated risk.
